question: The 6 samples here are raw paired-end FASTQ reads that have not been quantified — there is no gene/transcript count matrix. Answering "which genes are differentially expressed" requires a quantification step (alignment to GRCh38 + gene counting, e.g. STAR/HISAT2+featureCounts, or pseudo-alignment, e.g. Salmon/kallisto) before any DE testing (DESeq2/PyDESeq2) can run. I checked the sandbox's package census specifically for this: no aligner or pseudo-aligner is importable in Python or R (STAR, HISAT2, BWA, minimap2, Salmon, kallisto, Subread/featureCounts, Bowtie2 are all absent), and `list_available_packages(language="cli")` returns zero installable CLI tools — nothing can be added at runtime. A GRCh38 GENCODE v50 GTF is present under refs, but no genome/transcriptome FASTA or prebuilt index is visible, and more fundamentally there is no software in this environment able to convert FASTQ reads into counts. Please provide either (a) a pre-computed gene- or transcript-level count/abundance matrix for these 6 samples, or (b) confirmation that a quantification tool (STAR, Salmon, kallisto, or HISAT2+featureCounts) will be provisioned in the bulk-transcriptomics-agent's sandbox, so the plan can include a real quantification step rather than one that references software that isn't there.
